chapter: Recording dates, Goodman and band life
title: The 1958 jazz photograph in Harlem
summary: Jones recalls getting a call from Nat Hentoff, Milt Hinton's color film and standing with Horace Silver, Basie and the Joneses.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: as that." You know. We had some books open here, and one of "The Esquire Jazz Book," and it has an introduction them is (Inaudible) of that famous photograph in Harlem of all the jazzmen.
Yes. Yes.
You told me you were going to tell me about that day.
Oh, yes. Well, I don't know what other pictures they have in there. In the original Esquire book they had a whole two pages to Charlie Parker, and I don't know whether they have it here or not.
No, they don't have it on here. I have that, the original, but we were looking at this --
And then they had another page or so to Duke, you know?
Uh-huh.

Well, I just got this call, you know how New York is, you get a phone call you don't know what it is or how important it's going to be. There's no big production about anything, you know. So I got a -- I think Nat Hentoff called me and told me where to be. I was there and I saw all of these musicians, you know, getting together. Had no idea what it was about. And I think Milt Hinton, the great bass player, took movies of everybody moving about, color movies.
I think you said Milt showed them to you.

Oh, yes, they were great, you know? And I think Sonny Greer was moving around, talking. You could see him clowning. Because they're sounds. You know he had sound tracks on them. And let me see, what else can I think about that day.
Well, how long did it take to get the picture together, to get everybody lined up and up the steps of the --
Reasonably fast. It was surprising. Because anytime you can get all these drunks together --
(Laughter)
And everybody in there is -- we had -- you know how the pattern is. But they got them together.
What happened afterward? Did anybody get together musically?
No. We just went on back home and went on about our ways, you know?
You've got the makings of some great music there.

Oh, yes. Very prominent people. Very great talents. In fact I have at home some pictures of -- I don't know who took these. They were taken on the stairs. I think I was talking to Horace Silver and Basie and Jo Jones and Hank Jones and I were talking together, you know?
Uh-huh.
I have them at home. And -- somebody else was taking pictures that day, you know? But they must have known that this was going to come off. I didn't know until the last minute, you know?
